phases.journal: Ridgemere's bakers, healers, clerks and dockers want a paw with the day's work. Ask them, or read the city board.

effect.reply: Wherever the masts are. The pier under the Grayrock office, mostly. Follow your nose, eh? She smells of schoolroom chalk and the coal I keep in my pocket for luck.

effect.reply: The family and Timberland aren't speaking, so the kitchen cooks for one House and feeds the gossip of two. We don't take sides down here. We take plates.
The Houses have fallen out, and the family's at the windows all day watching who calls on whom. The kitchen just counts the plates coming back.
Upstairs is the steward's business, and the family's. Down here we know the price of eggs and which lanes flood first. That's enough knowing for anyone.

triggers.note: Reads nh_stage and nh_b_quarrel and nh_b_peace only to colour a line (decisions 7.1): greatly_grayrock is this House's quarrel. With the peace kept, the quiet line plays.

effect.reply: The Hall and Greatly are at each other's throats. Every Greatly cart that passes the gate gets a look from the steward that'd curdle milk. I just fold the sheets.
The Houses have fallen out, and the Hall's doors are shut to callers half the day. More sheets to fold, and fewer feet to dirty them.
Upstairs is upstairs. The family's away more than it's home, and the steward keeps the keys. Down here we keep the rain out, or try.

effect.words: How is it up at the Court?
effect.reply: The Court and Fellhall have fallen out over the timber, and the steward has us counting every log in the woodstore. I count. Nobody notices.

effect.words: How is it up at the Court?
effect.reply: The Houses have all fallen out, and the Court's doors are barred to half the city. The bolts still need carrying, mind.

effect.words: How is it up at the Court?
effect.reply: Upstairs is the steward's worry. Down here we worry about the damp, and the damp doesn't take sides.

quests.title: Morning Bread for the Sump
quests.summary: Carry the Morning Oven's first loaves down the Sump Stairs to the nurse at the Sump Infirmary.

offer.ask: You've flour to your elbows. Something wanted?
offer.say: #greet#. The first loaves go down to the Sump Infirmary every morning, and my carrier's off his feet. Four loaves to the nurse there, still warm if you're quick. Take the Sump Stairs, not the lanes; the lanes flood first. Will you?
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Warm bread for the sick, and not a loaf dropped. Take a cake for the walk. Same again tomorrow, if your paws are willing.

objectives.label: Give the four loaves to the nurse at the Sump Infirmary.
Get them there before the tenth hour, while they are warm.

quests.title: Herbs for the House of Mending
quests.summary: The abbey's House of Mending goes through herbs faster than its garden grows them.

offer.ask: Is the abbey short of something?
offer.say: #greet#. The House of Mending goes through herbs faster than the abbey garden grows them. Five bunches, from the long grass outside the walls or under the willows. Yarrow too, if you find it. I'll not ask where you picked them.
offer.handIn: Your herbs, and yarrow if I found it.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. That's the week's draughts. If you come in hurt one day, I'll remember whose herbs these were. That's more than I promise most.

objectives.label: Bring the healer five bunches of herbs.
Find two sprigs of yarrow for the poultices.

quests.title: Gone to See the Ships
quests.summary: The old wolf above the pawnshop has lost his littlest to the ships again. Find her and walk her home.

offer.ask: You look like you've lost something.
offer.say: #greet#, #address#. My littlest slipped her lessons again. She'll be down at the water counting masts; she always is. My knees won't take the Sump Stairs twice in a day. Would you find my minnow and walk her home, eh?
offer.thanks: There's my minnow. #thanks#, #address#. The patrolman on the Sump round used to walk her home, before he went up the Hundred Steps to keep the Palace lamp. Now it's you. #farewell#.

objectives.label: Find his pup on the piers.
Walk her back to her father.

quests.title: Oak Smoke for the Herring
quests.summary: The herring is in at the North Wharf smokehouse and its fires are low.

offer.ask: Your fires look low.
offer.say: #greet#. The herring's in and my fires are low. Three armfuls of firewood, and two strips of oak bark for the flavour. Oak, mind, not pine; pine smoke makes the fish taste of a ship's hold. The broad-leaved trees past the walls have both.
offer.accept: Oak, not pine. I'll bring it.
offer.handIn: Wood and oak bark, as you asked.
offer.thanks: That'll smoke sweet. #thanks#. Take a fish; it's this week's. Eat it while the Houses are still speaking to each other. I don't think they will be by winter.

objectives.label: Bring three armfuls of firewood.
Bring two strips of oak bark.

quests.title: Resin for the Tar Pot
quests.summary: The Ropewalk's tar pot wants pine resin, and the Grayrock ships take every fathom of rope it makes.

offer.ask: What's that smell? Tar?
offer.say: #greet#. Tar, and not enough of it. An untarred rope rots on its first wet voyage. Three lumps of pine resin for the pot, from the pines up in the hills. And a lump of beeswax, if the chandlers can spare one, for whipping the ends.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Into the pot it goes, and into the steward's book to the lump. Take a coil; tarred, it'll outlast us both. The Grayrock ships take every fathom I make.

objectives.label: Bring three lumps of pine resin.
Bring a lump of beeswax for whipping the rope ends.

quests.title: A Page and a Drawer
quests.summary: The copyists at the Records Office are a paw short. Copy a page and sort a drawer.

offer.ask: Are they short of paws up there?
offer.say: #greet#. The copyists are a paw short and the rolls don't wait. Copy me one page and sort me one drawer. The Office pays by the page, and you'll read things up there nobody downstairs remembers.
offer.handIn: The page is copied and the drawer sorted.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Square letters, too; I can tell a careless paw a room away. You'd be surprised what's in those drawers. A whole village struck off in one line, the spring after a flood. Come again.

objectives.label: Copy a page at the Records Office.
Sort a drawer of old rolls.
Sort one more drawer, and find the drowned village's page in the old count.

bonus.text: Under the drowned village's name, someone has written: struck from the rolls, the spring after the flood. Nothing else.

quests.title: The Heights Round
quests.summary: Carry a City Office letter up the hill to the wolf who keeps the Vance house's door.

offer.ask: Is the City Office sending something up the hill?
offer.say: #greet#. The City Office's letters for the Heights pile up on my desk, because nobody likes the climb or the looks at the door. This one's for the Vance house, to the wolf who keeps their door. My knees did that hill for forty years. They've retired, even if I haven't.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. One less on the pile, and one less climb for me. Half the Heights owes a House factor, and they'd sooner not open anything with a seal on it. You got one opened. That's a day's work, that is.

objectives.label: Give the letter to the Vances' doorkeeper.

quests.title: Candles for Restday
quests.summary: On Restday the cathedral burns more candles than the abbey can pour. Bring two, and come to the service.

offer.ask: Is there work for a pair of paws here?
offer.say: #greet#. On Restday this cathedral burns more candles than the abbey can pour. Bring me two, wax or tallow, and come to the Restday service between the ninth hour and the eleventh. The Bright One sees who fills the lamps, and so do I.
offer.accept: Two candles, and I'll be there.
offer.handIn: Candles, and I came to the service.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. The old King's candle is still lit by the altar. We've not let it go out since he went up. Yours will stand beside it, and I'll count them with the bells.

objectives.label: Bring the sexton two candles, wax or tallow.
Come into the cathedral for the Restday service, between the ninth hour and the eleventh.

quests.title: The Almoner's Round
quests.summary: Carry the abbey's alms bread down to the Wharf and the Sump: a loaf each to three wolves, and no questions asked.

offer.ask: You're carrying a lot of bread.
offer.say: #greet#. The abbey's alms go down to the Sump and I can't carry them all. Three loaves, one each, to three wolves on the Wharf side who look like they need it. Don't ask them why. A full net's no shame to share, eh?
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Three fed. Back home the lake gives to whoever puts a net in. The Sump never had a lake, so it has us. #farewell#.

objectives.label: Give a loaf each to three wolves on the Wharf and in the Sump.
Share a meal with someone in the Sump.

quests.title: Marketday Stock
quests.summary: Marketday empties the Market Hall provisioner's shelves by noon. Sell her three things you've gathered.

offer.ask: Your shelves look bare.
offer.say: #greet#. Marketday empties my shelves by noon. Sell me three of anything good you've gathered: mushrooms, berries, herbs. I'll pay an honest price and a little over. And if you've the nerve, rent a stall on the Square on Marketday and see how the other half lives.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Fair dealing. Half the Square owes the Counting House this month, so it's nice to trade with someone who doesn't flinch at a coin. I've a letter for a lord who's never home, if you ever see him.

objectives.label: Sell the provisioner three goods you have gathered.
Rent a stall on Market Square on Marketday.

quests.title: Greens for the Rag Market
quests.summary: The greens stall in the Rag Market is a basket short. City wolves buy mushrooms above all.

offer.ask: What sells best on this stall?
offer.say: #greet#, #address#. City wolves'll buy any green thing, mm? Mushrooms most of all. Four, from the deadwood and the ferns in the woods past the walls. A few berries too, for colour, if it's the season. Back home in the Rainwood I'd have a basket by breakfast.
offer.thanks: Good bark, these. #thanks#. Have yesterday's stew, mm? It's better the second day, like most things. And every penny the stall makes goes to the factor by the new moon.

objectives.label: Bring four mushrooms.
Bring two handfuls of berries for colour.

quests.title: Charcoal for the Nail-Hearths
quests.summary: The Nailers' Forge in the Cinders eats charcoal faster than Timberland sends it.

offer.ask: Those hearths look hungry.
offer.say: #greet#. The nail-hearths eat charcoal like the Houses eat coin. Three sacks from the Timberland charcoal store, on the Sump side of the Commons, and I'll keep the fires in through Emberday. Timberland pays, eventually. Timberland always pays eventually.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Take a paw of nails; we make more than we sell. And if anyone from another House asks what you saw down here, you saw a forge. That's all there is to see.

objectives.label: Bring the smith three sacks of charcoal.

quests.title: Oats for the Factors' Horses
quests.summary: The Greatly stables want oats and straw: the factors will soon be riding their debt rounds.

offer.ask: Do the Greatly horses want feeding?
offer.say: #greet#. Greatly horses eat better than half the Sump, and I'm the one feeds them. Three of oats and two bundles of straw. Any provisioner has oats; for straw, try the sundries shop in the Sump. The factors want the horses fresh for the debt rounds, chalk in their pouches.
offer.accept: Oats and straw. I'll fetch it.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Don't look so sour. Whoever owns the horse, it's the horse that's hungry. I grew up on a charcoal camp; I know what it is to work for a House and keep your own counsel.

objectives.label: Bring three of oats.
Bring two bundles of straw for bedding.

quests.title: The Dawn Bell
quests.summary: Nobody has rung the Clock Tower bell at first light since the old King went up. Ring it, and tell the lamplighter.

offer.ask: Who rings the morning bell these days?
offer.say: #greet#. I light the lamps at dusk and put them out at first light, and since the old King went up nobody rings the morning bell. The rope's at the top of the Clock Tower stair. Ring it between the fifth hour and the seventh, and come and tell me.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. I heard it from here. There's wolves in the Sump who set their day by that bell, and they've been late ever since he went up. I had a post once that mattered. This is a small thing, but it's mine to see done.

objectives.label: Climb the Clock Tower and ring the bell at first light, between the fifth hour and the seventh.
Tell the lamplighter the bell is rung.

quests.title: Take Her Lines
quests.summary: Be on the piers while a ship is in to take her lines, and bring a coil of rope for the bollards.

offer.ask: You look like you're waiting for something.
offer.say: #greet#, #address#. When a ship comes in, somebody has to be on the pier to take her lines, and the Grayrock office never sends enough paws. Be on the piers when the next one's in, and bring me a coil of rope for the bollards. The notice by the office says which day she's due.
offer.handIn: She's tied up, and here's your rope.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Snug as a pup in a basket. I'll be up in the Heights one day, you know, a house with a door that sticks. And I'll still come down to take a ship's lines.

objectives.label: Be on the piers while a ship is in, and take her lines.
Bring the docker a coil of rope for the bollards.

quests.title: A Crate Light
quests.summary: The Oakhaven wagon went out a crate light. Carry it along the Sound Road to Oakhaven Stores.

offer.ask: Is that crate going somewhere?
offer.say: #greet#. The Oakhaven wagon went out a crate light, and the storekeeper there counts everything twice. Carry it along the Sound Road to Oakhaven Stores, would you? It's not heavy. It's just far, and the road's not as safe as it was.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. He'll have counted it twice and found it right, for once. Roads are like the Houses, mind: never quite where you left them.

objectives.label: Carry the crate to the Oakhaven storekeeper.

quests.title: Willow Bark for the Heights' Joints
quests.summary: The damp has got into every old joint in the Heights. The wolf who visits the sick there trusts willow bark.

offer.ask: Who's ailing up here?
offer.say: #greet#. The damp's got into every old joint in the Heights, and the good houses would sooner send for a physician than for bark. I've more faith in willow. Three strips of willow bark from any physic on the Commons, or willow tea if they've some made.
offer.thanks: #thanks#, #address#. Steeped tonight, and three old wolves on this street will take their stairs tomorrow without swearing at them. My cousin in the Fell vineyards swears by it for the pickers' backs.

objectives.label: Bring three strips of willow bark, or willow tea.

quests.title: Pheasants for the Cinder Butchers
quests.summary: The Heights want pheasant pie and the Cinder butcher's hooks are bare. Two birds out of the Rainward Woods.

offer.ask: Hooks are looking bare.
offer.say: #greet#, #address#. The Heights want pheasant pie and my hooks are bare. Two birds out of the Rainward Woods, past Fellhall, eh? They'd sooner run than fly; head them off. And the feathers, if you keep them. I sell those too.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Fair catch, both. Here's a pie from yesterday's batch. Next time you're down by the Sound, ask me the name of any ship you see, eh? I know them all.

objectives.label: Take two pheasants in the Rainward Woods, either side of Fellhall.
Bring the butcher the feathers.

quests.title: Sounding the Tarns
quests.summary: Soundings is redrawing the Rainward Hills. Walk out to Rainmere and Slate Tarn and say they are where the chart says.

offer.ask: What are all those charts?
offer.say: #greet#. The cartographer's redrawing the hills and wants to know the tarns are where the old chart says. Walk out to Rainmere and on to Slate Tarn, then come back and tell me they're still there. They will be. It's the roads between that keep moving.
offer.handIn: Both tarns are where the chart says.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. She'll be pleased. She's marking every hill a howl could carry from, though she won't say why. Highmere's the one the chart's least sure of, if you ever get that far.

objectives.label: Walk out to Rainmere.
Walk on to Slate Tarn.
Tell the chart-keeper what you saw.
Go on as far as Highmere.
If you have the Sound Gift, use its Echo at Slate Tarn.

quests.title: Eggs for the Fellhall Kitchen
quests.summary: The Fellhall kitchen is short for the family's supper. Four eggs and two cheeses from the Commons, round the back.

offer.ask: Does the kitchen want something fetched?
offer.say: #greet#. The cook's short for the family's supper and won't send me to market twice. Four eggs and two cheeses from the Commons, brought round to the kitchens. Keep to the high side of the street; the low side floods first. I'd go myself, but the hall doesn't sweep itself.
offer.accept: Eggs and cheese, round the back.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Eggs whole and the cheese not sat on. The cook will think I went myself. I was born in the Sump, you know. One day I'll have a kitchen in the Heights and a hall servant of my own to send.

objectives.label: Bring the hall servant four eggs.
Bring two cheeses.
Come in by the kitchens, not the front door.

quests.title: Clean Linen for Grayrock Hall
quests.summary: The family's linen came back from the washers grey with sea damp. The chambers want fresh on every bed.

offer.ask: Is the Hall short of something?
offer.say: #greet#! The family's linen came back from the washers grey with sea damp, and the chamber keeper wants fresh on every bed before anyone upstairs notices. Two lengths of linen cloth from the stores, and lavender for the presses if the season's left any.
offer.thanks: #thanks#! Every bed made before the bell. Take a candle; the chambers burn more than they need. I'll watch the rain stop one day, you'll see. Then I'll have nothing to do but fold.

objectives.label: Bring two lengths of linen cloth.
Bring two sprigs of lavender for the linen presses.

quests.title: A Bolt for the Court
quests.summary: Greywool has finished the Court's winter hangings. Carry the bolt to the chamber keeper at Timberland Court.

offer.ask: Is that bolt going somewhere?
offer.say: #greet#. Greywool's finished the Court's winter hangings, and I can't carry the bolt and keep my place at the loom. Take it to the chamber keeper at Timberland Court. He takes his supper in the servants' hall, and he hums, so you'll find him.
offer.handIn: The bolt's with the chamber keeper.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. He'll have hummed at it and counted the ells twice. And if you brought wood for the hall fire, thank you for that too. The damp in that hall could drown a fish.

objectives.label: Give the bolt to the Court's chamber keeper.
Bring two armfuls of firewood for the servants' hall fire, against the damp.
